blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] docs/storytime/l2-unit2/w*/muse/l2-w*-check-row-*.json linePrompt (64 specs, 16 new rows): every check-row linePrompt is the unit 1 bus text: 'The bus body, the wheels, and each window are separate closed shapes' and 'This object has no eyes and no face: draw no eyes, no pupils, and no face anywhere'. l2-w10-check-row-dad and l2-w15-check-row-girl say 'one object' for a person, and l2-w14-check-row-foot says 'one object' for a body part (the R5 fix reached only the colorPrompt). The new rows doll, duck, elephant, horse, and goat have faces, so the paid line-art call would remove eyes and face. Unit 1 l2-w07-check-row-cat has its own cat rule with eyes and pupil. Fix: object-specific or person-form line rules, no bus sentence, face rule only for an object without a face; rerun the maker, the test, and the hand-off build.
nonblocking_findings: F2 [Major] docs/storytime/l2-unit2/w12/muse l2-w12-* hen rows (6 rows) and w13 pot rows (8 rows): the Forge reference out/chicken/views/three-quarter.png shows a WHITE hen, but the colorPrompt says 'ONE small brown hen ... draw the same object with the same shape and colors', so the paid call gets two colors. The text says 'three times (side, three-quarter, front)' (hen) and 'three times (front, three-quarter, top)' (pot), but the reference file holds one view. The pot render shows a plant with red flowers; the text says 'round clay flower pot' with no plant. Decide: change the text to match the render, or use a new element sheet.

Farmyard story pages say 'a low camera height in the room' and carry the Mom and Tom proportion sentences with no Mom or Tom. The 'Exactly the characters named here' sentence limits the effect, so low risk.
